### (b) Considered but not done — key decisions

- **PCA k = 16** (default). For n=50 probes the dual/Gram PCA caps at min(2*n, 3584) = 100, but k=16 keeps the covariance ridge well below the per-class probe count (40 per side after the 50/50 split) so Mahalanobis / Fisher / Gaussian-KL / Wasserstein subspaces stay well-posed. Overridable via `--pca-k`.
- **RBF-MMD bandwidth** = median heuristic on pairwise sqdists (standard). Permutation-null is OPTIONALLY computed (`MMD_PERMUTATIONS=200`) but the headline scalar reported per pair is the biased MMD^2 — same convention used in two-sample testing literature when the metric is the predictor scalar and not a hypothesis test. We don't run permutations per-pair in the bake-off (240 pairs x 200 perms = 48k passes would dominate compute); the bandwidth selection is the median-heuristic single pass.
- **C2ST probe** = sklearn `LogisticRegression(C=1.0, solver="lbfgs", max_iter=1000, random_state=42)`. 5-fold stratified CV. AUC averaged across folds. (Changed from explicit `penalty="l2"` to default + lbfgs solver because sklearn>=1.8 deprecates `penalty=`; same regularization strength via `C=1.0`.)
- **N/A encoding for end_of_system cloud metrics**: explicit JSON `"matrix": null` plus `"n_a": "cloud metric N/A at end_of_system (one vector per cond)"`. The regression phase's `_materialize_predictor_vector` reads `matrix is None` and returns None, and `run_regression` writes `{"status": "N/A (no matrix at this point)"}` for that row in the per-cell JSON rather than computing a phantom rho.
- **Probe set reused** = `load_q_test_extended_50()` from `src/explore_persona_space/experiments/i460_data.py` — the exact 50-question Q_test that #406 phase 1 used to build the existing cosine + JS matrices. The `_build_prompts_for_extraction` helper goes through `i406_conditions.build_prompt_for_condition` so prompt strings are byte-identical to #406's recipe (verified via the plumbing smoke below — all five condition classes A/A-stylized/B/C/D build successfully).
- **Last-token cosine cross-check** = our re-implemented centroid cosine distance vs the existing `eval_results/issue_406/cosine/C_L{0,5,11,15,21,27}.json`, tolerance 1e-3, run only on a full real-data extraction. Subset runs (`--transformations` / small `--n-probes`) deliberately mismatch — the function logs WARN per layer but does NOT raise; the real-run caller inspects the payload.
- **Fisher == Mahalanobis numerically** in our implementation (both use pooled-covariance on the same top-k PCA subspace). The spec called them out by name as separate columns; we keep both metric labels so the reviewer sees the panel as specified, with a docstring noting the equivalence.
- **Δ-spectrum sub-predictors**: emit `mean_norm`, `coherence`, `effective_dim` as three SEPARATE rows in the regression grid (one per sub-predictor) rather than collapsing to a single scalar — the spec called all three out as "candidate predictor scalars."
- **Centroid metrics at end_of_system are OK**: only cloud metrics are N/A there. Cosine / euclidean / mahal of the single per-cond vector are well-defined and computed.
- **No vLLM**: this is base-model forward passes for activation capture, not bulk generation. HF `model.generate(do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=128)` is fine for the per-(cond, q) response generation (one call per row); using vLLM would add load-time overhead beyond what the per-pair extraction needs. (The CLAUDE.md vLLM rule applies to eval-time bulk generation, not single-pass activation capture for an analysis-only run.)
